No theorem is claimed in positive characteristic, for a=0, for rational or Laurent maps, or for arbitrary polynomial automorphisms.
Actual collected support is not claimed invariant under affine conjugacy.
Finite rank is not replaced by finite generation or bounded torsion; arbitrary torsion, including mu_infinity when present, remains allowed.
The article does not improve the earlier companion's explicit planar nonzero-constant cardinality bounds.
The bounded primary-source comparison is not a global, exhaustive, first-result, or unpublished-work claim.
Part A does not classify all equality cosets or all maximal cosets.

laurent_bridge_lock.arbitrary_characteristic_zero: Generate L over Q by the finitely many map coefficients and generators of Gamma_0; L embeds in C. Every gamma in Gamma is algebraic over L, so extend the embedding to an algebraic closure containing the relevant points. Never claim an embedding of all K.
laurent_bridge_lock.arbitrary_finite_rank: Choose gamma_1,...,gamma_r whose tensor classes form a Q-basis and Gamma_0=<gamma_1,...,gamma_r>. For each gamma, an integral rational relation makes gamma^N times a Gamma_0 element torsion; kill the finite order of that individual torsion element to obtain gamma^(NM) in Gamma_0. Thus Gamma is contained elementwise in Gamma_0^div.
laurent_bridge_lock.arbitrary_torsion: No finite-generation or bounded-torsion assumption; the elementwise argument includes arbitrary infinite torsion and mu_infinity because each torsion element has finite order and belongs to the division hull of the identity.
laurent_bridge_lock.geometric_transfer: Use Cartesian powers; absence of a positive-dimensional torus coset is preserved by the chosen embedding and injectivity transfers finiteness back.
laurent_bridge_lock.imported_statement: For a closed subvariety X of a complex algebraic torus and the division group Lambda^div of a finitely generated subgroup Lambda, X intersect Lambda^div is a finite union of intersections with torus cosets contained in X.
laurent_bridge_lock.journal_source: Michel Laurent, Inventiones mathematicae 78 (1984), 299--327, DOI 10.1007/BF01388597, EuDML journal record 143175.
laurent_bridge_lock.quantitative_status: Qualitative only: no effective count, exceptional-set algorithm, height bound, or enumeration.
laurent_bridge_lock.used_corollary: If X contains no positive-dimensional torus coset, then X intersect Lambda^div is finite.

part_a.arithmetic_conclusion: For every characteristic-zero K, every stated anchored map over K, and every finite-rank Gamma<=K* with arbitrary torsion and no finite-generation assumption, T_k(S,Gamma) is finite; T_m is finite for every m>=k because T_m is a subset of T_k.
part_a.arithmetic_set: T_m(S,Gamma)={z in Gamma^k:S^j(z) in Gamma^k for every integer 0<=j<=m}. If z=(x_0,...,x_(k-1)), its time-j state is (x_j,...,x_(j+k-1)), and projection is a bijection V_m intersect Gamma^(k+m) -> T_m.
part_a.disconnected_extension: For xi D contained in V_m with D possibly disconnected, every component is a translate of D^0 contained in V_m and dim D=dim D^0<=k-m.
part_a.equality_statement: If a=1 and P(1)=0, R_m={n-nu mod k:0<=n<m}; H_m fixes x_r=1 for r in R_m and imposes x_(k+n)=x_n for 0<=n<m. It is saturated, connected, contained in V_m, and isomorphic to G_m^(k-m). These conditions are sufficient, not necessary.
part_a.field_and_parameters: Omega algebraically closed characteristic zero; k>=2; 1<=nu<=k-1; a nonzero; P(X)=c+sum_(j=1)^s b_j X^(e_j), 0<e_1<...<e_s, a,c,b_j nonzero, and s>=2 actual nonconstant support after collection/deletion.
part_a.geometric_statement: For every 0<=m<=k and every connected embedded subtorus H with xi H contained in V_m, dim H<=k-m.
part_a.no_gcd_statement: The killed initial residues are the translation R_m={n-nu mod k:0<=n<m}, with m distinct residues; it is not the orbit {-j nu mod k}, and no gcd(k,nu) condition occurs.
part_a.sharp_clock: For every prescribed s>=2 and every k,nu, take a=1,b_j=1,c=-s,Gamma=<2>. At m=k-1 the free residue q=k-1-nu has x_q=t, all other initial coordinates 1, and x_(k+n)=x_n; t=2^N gives infinite T_(k-1).
part_a.survivor_variety: V_m is the closed subvariety of G_m^(k+m), coordinates x_0,...,x_(k+m-1), cut out by x_(n+k)=P(x_(n+k-nu))+a x_n for 0<=n<m; V_0=G_m^k.
part_a.theorem_name: Anchored torus-coset dimension decay and sharp finite-rank clock

part_b.arithmetic_conclusion: For every characteristic-zero K and finite-rank Gamma<=K* with arbitrary torsion, T_2 is finite for every nonlinear support off the resonant {1,d} locus; on resonant {1,d}, T_3 is finite. Linear E={1} is excluded and may remain infinite for every window. All conclusions are qualitative.
part_b.exceptional_support: For E={1,d}, d>=2, P(X)=beta X+delta X^d, V_2^0 contains a positive-dimensional connected torus coset iff a=-beta^2. Then the unique connected positive-dimensional coset is C_d={((delta/beta^2)t^d,t,beta t,delta beta^d t^d):t in G_m}. For every coefficients, including resonance, V_3^0 has no positive-dimensional torus coset.
part_b.field_and_parameters: Omega algebraically closed characteristic zero; k=2; nu=1; c=0; a nonzero; P(X)=sum_(e in E)b_e X^e for nonempty finite actual support E of positive integers and every b_e nonzero.
part_b.geometric_arithmetic_separation: C_d existence does not imply infinite T_2 for every Gamma; beta=delta=1,a=-1,Gamma=<2> gives (t^d,t,t,t^d) and infinite T_2.
part_b.linear_support: For E={1}, P(X)=beta X, any nonzero r with r^2=beta r+a gives {(t,rt,...,r^(m+1)t):t in G_m} contained in V_m^0 for every m. The compatible beta=2,a=-1,r=1,Gamma=<2> family is infinite in every window.
part_b.other_nonlinear_supports: For nonlinear monomial E={d}, d>=2; every binomial E={p,q}, 2<=p<q; and every |E|>=3, V_2^0 contains no positive-dimensional torus coset. Every nonlinear support has no positive-dimensional torus coset in V_3^0.
part_b.recurrence: x_(n+2)=P(x_(n+1))+a x_n; specifically x_2=P(x_1)+a x_0, x_3=P(x_2)+a x_1, x_4=P(x_3)+a x_2.
part_b.survivor_variety: V_m^0 is the closed subvariety of G_m^(m+2), coordinates x_0,...,x_(m+1), cut out by x_(n+2)=P(x_(n+1))+a x_n for 0<=n<m.
part_b.theorem_name: Exact zero-constant planar support and resonance phase
